newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Trade groups slams EU cotton anti-dumping inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Trade groups slams EU cotton anti-dumping inquiry.

text.p: A leading trade group has slammed a European Commission decision to reopen inquiries into alleged dumping of unbleached cotton from Asia, accusing a textile lobby group of deliberate harassment.

EuroCommerce, which represents European retail and wholesale interests, said in a statement that the Commission urgently needed to look at introducing trade legislation that prevented "chain complaints".
"(The anti-dumping inquiry) constitutes nothing less than deliberate trade harassment from the side of EuroCoton," the statement said.
On Thursday the Commission reopened inquiries into alleged dumping of unbleached cotton imports from six countries, setting the stage for another internal tussle over the bloc's anti-dumping tactics.

The inquiries into grey cotton fabric from China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Pakistan and Turkey follows a complaint by EuroCoton, the Committee of the Cotton and allied Textile Industries of the European Union.
It reopens a file closed only last May when a majority of EU trade ministers rejected the Commission's case for setting definitive dumping duties against the same six countries.
EuroCoton reacted furiously at the time, saying the ministers had acted unlawfully and vowing to consider legal action in the European Court of Justice.
The measures ministers rejected would have hit imports from the six named countries worth 379 million European currency units ($424 million) in 1995.

Those proposals would have hit Chinese-origin imports with 18.9 percent duties, those from Egypt with 13 percent, India 17.2 percent, Indonesia 14.5 percent, Pakistan 22.9 percent and Turkey 17.5 percent.

EuroCommerce urged the Commission to rethink its trade regulations, saying: "To prevent abuse, it is imperative to introduce a trade harassment clause which stipulates that a complaint can only be accepted if a very similar complaint by the same complainants regarding a very similar product has not been rejected before.
EuroCommerce said that in the past two years EuroCoton alone had filed three complaints on grey cotton fabrics and two on cotton-type bed linen.
A EuroCoton spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
